title: Nova Biomedical StatStrip Blood Glucose Meter - Strip Not Recognized or Insertion Errors
description: Troubleshooting strip detection failures and insertion errors on the StatStrip blood glucose meter.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot while actively testing a patient sample. Move testing to another meter if available.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error Message
steps.instructions: Power on the device and insert a test strip. Confirm the exact error (e.g., “Strip Not Recognized” or insertion error).

steps.title: Check Test Strip Compatibility and Lot
steps.instructions: Ensure the strips are correct for the StatStrip system and not mixed with another model or vendor. Verify correct strip type and confirm lot is approved for use.

steps.title: Inspect Strip Expiration and Storage Conditions
steps.instructions: Check expiration date and confirm strips were stored per manufacturer guidelines (sealed container, proper temperature/humidity).

steps.title: Inspect Strip Insertion Technique
steps.instructions: Insert the strip fully and in the correct orientation. Ensure contacts are facing the correct direction and avoid partial insertion.

steps.title: Check for Contamination or Debris in Strip Port
steps.instructions: Visually inspect the strip port for dirt, dried fluid, or obstructed contacts. Clean gently per approved methods.

steps.title: Try a New Test Strip from a Different Vial
steps.instructions: Insert a strip from a new vial or different lot to determine if the issue is strip-related.

steps.title: Check Meter Battery and Power Stability
steps.instructions: Ensure the battery is adequately charged or properly seated. Replace or reseat if needed.

steps.title: Restart the Device
steps.instructions: Power cycle the meter and attempt strip insertion again.

steps.title: Test with Known Good Conditions
steps.instructions: Use a known good strip, proper insertion, and confirmed good battery to verify consistent recognition.

CCR.Complaint: Meter not recognizing test strips during routine glucose testing.
CCR.Cause: Contaminated strip port preventing proper contact with test strips.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned strip port and verified proper strip recognition with new vial of strips.

helpfulDetails: Final device status (returned to service or sent for repair)

title: Nova Biomedical StatStrip Blood Glucose Meter - Connectivity or Download Failure
description: Failure to transmit results, docking issues, or inability to download data due to network, docking, or configuration problems.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not delay critical glucose testing due to connectivity issues. Use another functioning meter if needed and manually document results per policy.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact symptom such as meter not uploading results, dock not recognizing meter, wireless icon errors, or data stuck in queue.

steps.title: Check Docking Station Connection (Most Common Cause)
steps.instructions: Ensure dock has power, Ethernet is connected, and try a known working port. Dock the meter and observe syncing behavior.

steps.title: Inspect Meter Dock Contacts
steps.instructions: Check contacts for dirt, corrosion, or damage and clean if needed. Re-dock and test.

steps.title: Check Network Availability
steps.instructions: Verify Ethernet link lights and network access or confirm wireless settings if applicable.

steps.title: Restart the Meter
steps.instructions: Power cycle the meter and re-dock after reboot.

steps.title: Check for Stored Data Backlog
steps.instructions: Attempt manual upload or sync and observe for error messages.

steps.title: Verify Configuration / Device Assignment
steps.instructions: Confirm correct unit ID, system registration, and that the device is active in middleware.

steps.title: Swap with Known Working Components
steps.instructions: Test with another dock or meter to isolate whether the issue follows the device or docking station.

CCR.Complaint: StatStrip meter not uploading glucose results to system when docked.
CCR.Cause: Faulty docking station Ethernet connection preventing network communication.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced docking station and verified successful data upload.

helpfulDetails: Dock power and network status verified
Final device status (working, removed from service, sent for repair)

title: Nova Biomedical StatStrip Blood Glucose Meter - QC Lockout or Control Failures
description: Troubleshooting QC lockout conditions preventing testing due to failed, expired, or incomplete quality control checks.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not attempt patient testing while the meter is in QC lockout. Obtain another functioning meter for patient care.

steps.title: Confirm QC Lockout Message
steps.instructions: Power on the meter and verify the displayed message such as QC required, QC failed, or lockout warning.

steps.title: Check QC Due Status and Timing
steps.instructions: Navigate to QC status, check last successful QC date and time, and compare with facility QC policy.

steps.title: Verify QC Materials
steps.instructions: Inspect QC solution and test strips for expiration, proper storage, and correct QC level.

steps.title: Perform QC Test Properly
steps.instructions: Insert strip correctly, apply QC solution properly, and avoid contamination.

steps.title: Check Strip Lot and Coding
steps.instructions: Ensure strips match expected lot, verify vial matches configuration, and confirm no strip damage.

steps.title: Inspect Meter Contacts and Strip Port
steps.instructions: Check for debris or contamination and clean per approved procedure if needed.

steps.title: Check Docking and Connectivity
steps.instructions: Ensure proper docking and confirm communication with data system if QC upload is required.

steps.title: Restart the Meter
steps.instructions: Power cycle the device after successful QC to clear lockout.

CCR.Complaint: Meter in QC lockout and unable to perform patient testing.
CCR.Cause: Expired QC solution causing repeated QC failures and lockout condition.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced QC materials, performed successful QC, and restored meter to service.

helpfulDetails: Meter docking and upload status confirmed
Final device status (returned to service or removed)

title: Nova Biomedical StatStrip Glucose Monitor System - Battery Not Charging or Docking Failure
description: Meter not charging, low battery despite docking, or no charging indicator when placed in base station.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the meter from clinical use if battery is critically low or unreliable. Use a backup device for patient testing. Expected: No patient care interruption Why it matters: Power loss during testing can delay care or cause inaccurate documentation

steps.title: Verify Charging Indicator Behavior
steps.instructions: Place the StatStrip in the docking station and observe for charging indicators (LED or on-screen icon). Expected: Charging indicator appears within a few seconds Why it matters: Confirms whether the device recognizes the dock and is receiving power

steps.title: Check Power to Docking Station
steps.instructions: Ensure the docking station is plugged in and powered. Verify outlet functionality using another device. Expected: Dock has confirmed power Why it matters: A dead outlet or unplugged dock is a common and easily missed cause

steps.title: Inspect Docking Station Connections
steps.instructions: Check the power adapter connection to the dock and wall. Look for loose or damaged cables. Expected: All connections secure and intact Why it matters: Intermittent or failed connections prevent consistent charging

steps.title: Clean Charging Contacts (Common Issue)
steps.instructions: Inspect and clean the metal charging contacts on both the meter and the docking station using approved wipes (e.g., alcohol). Expected: Contacts are clean, dry, and free of residue Why it matters: Glucose meters frequently accumulate debris that blocks electrical contact

steps.title: Reseat the Meter in the Dock
steps.instructions: Remove and firmly reseat the meter in the docking station. Ensure it is properly aligned and fully seated. Expected: Charging indicator activates Why it matters: Misalignment prevents proper contact engagement

steps.title: Try a Known Good Dock or Meter
steps.instructions: Place the meter in a different working dock, or place a known working meter in the current dock. Expected: If meter charges in another dock → original dock is faulty If another meter fails in this dock → dock or power supply issue Why it matters: Isolates whether the issue is with the meter or docking station

steps.title: Check for Battery Age or Degradation
steps.instructions: If the meter only holds a charge briefly or fails to charge consistently, the internal battery may be worn. Expected: Battery maintains charge during normal use Why it matters: Rechargeable batteries degrade over time and eventually fail

steps.title: Restart the Meter
steps.instructions: Power cycle the device and return it to the dock. Expected: Charging resumes after reboot Why it matters: Clears minor software or charging recognition issues

CCR.Complaint: StatStrip meter not charging in docking station; battery remains low.
CCR.Cause: Dirty charging contacts preventing electrical connection.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned contacts and verified proper charging function in dock.

helpfulDetails: Results with alternate dock or meter
Final device status (returned to service or sent out)

title: Nova Biomedical StatStrip Blood Glucose Meter - Display or Button Errors
description: Troubleshooting unresponsive buttons, display issues, or frozen screens on the StatStrip meter.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the device from active patient use and transition testing to a backup meter to avoid delays in care.

steps.title: Inspect for Physical Damage
steps.instructions: Check the screen and keypad for cracks, fluid intrusion, or visible wear. If damage is present, remove from service.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Device
steps.instructions: Turn the meter off, wait 10 seconds, and turn it back on. If resolved, return to service.

steps.title: Check Battery Status and Connections
steps.instructions: Ensure the battery is properly seated and charged. Replace with a known-good battery if needed.

steps.title: Inspect and Clean the Keypad Area
steps.instructions: Look for dried fluids, glucose residue, or debris around buttons. Clean using approved disinfectant wipes.

steps.title: Test Button Responsiveness
steps.instructions: Press each button individually and observe response on screen to determine if issue is isolated or systemic.

steps.title: Check Screen Functionality
steps.instructions: Observe for dim display, missing segments, flickering, or distortion. Adjust brightness/settings if available.

steps.title: Verify Software/Interface Behavior
steps.instructions: Navigate menus to confirm normal operation and identify software or hardware issues.

steps.title: Check Docking/Charging Station
steps.instructions: Ensure proper docking and communication if the unit syncs or charges via base.

CCR.Complaint: Glucose meter screen freezing and buttons not responding during use.
CCR.Cause: Buttons intermittently unresponsive due to contamination buildup around keypad.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned keypad and verified proper button function; device returned to service.

helpfulDetails: Final device status (in service or removed)

title: Nova Biomedical StatStrip Blood Glucose Meter - Sample Not Detected or Insufficient Sample Repeats
description: Repeated sample-detection failures caused by strip condition, sample application, contamination, technique, environmental conditions, or meter-side strip-port problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Care and Confirm the Reported Condition
steps.instructions: If glucose information is needed for immediate clinical decisions, have clinical staff use another verified meter or approved laboratory method while the affected StatStrip is evaluated. Confirm exactly what occurred, including whether the meter repeatedly failed to detect the sample, reported insufficient sample, or failed only with certain strips or users. Expected outcome: Patient testing continues safely and the exact failure pattern is identified. If the problem cannot be reproduced and the meter completes a valid test with approved controls or test materials as required by facility procedure, troubleshooting may stop after final verification.

steps.title: 2. Inspect the Test Strip
steps.instructions: Verify that the strip is the correct type for the StatStrip system and is not visibly damaged, bent, contaminated, wet, or improperly stored. Check the strip container and handling conditions according to facility and manufacturer requirements. Do not use questionable strips for troubleshooting. Expected outcome: A clean, undamaged, properly stored strip is available for testing. If replacing the suspect strip resolves the problem and functional verification passes, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Sample Application Conditions
steps.instructions: Observe whether the sample is being presented correctly to the strip without touching or contaminating the application area. Verify that sufficient sample is available and that the sample is not being partially applied and then reapplied after a delay. Clinical Engineering should evaluate whether the reported failure follows one particular collection method, accessory, or workflow rather than assuming a meter failure. Expected outcome: Proper sample presentation results in normal sample detection. If proper application resolves the repeated failure, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Check the Strip Port Externally
steps.instructions: Power down the meter if appropriate and inspect the strip port for visible blood, cleaning residue, debris, corrosion, bent material, foreign objects, or physical damage. Do not insert tools into the strip port or perform deep cleaning beyond approved external procedures. Expected outcome: The strip port is visibly clean, dry, unobstructed, and undamaged. If approved external cleaning resolves the problem and the meter passes verification testing, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 5. Try a Known-Good Strip Supply
steps.instructions: Using strips confirmed to be acceptable and properly stored, repeat the test under controlled conditions. If multiple meters are available, compare the suspect strip supply with another functioning StatStrip meter without mixing questionable consumables into clinical inventory. Expected outcome: Known-good strips are consistently recognized and accept the sample. If the meter works reliably with known-good strips, isolate and remove the suspect strip supply from use according to facility procedure.

steps.title: 6. Check Environmental and Handling Conditions
steps.instructions: Confirm that the meter and strips have not recently been exposed to excessive moisture, condensation, temperature extremes, liquid intrusion, or a rapid environmental change. Allow equipment and consumables to stabilize within approved operating conditions when applicable. Expected outcome: The meter and strips are dry, stable, and operating in an appropriate environment. If the failure disappears after environmental conditions are corrected and verification passes, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 7. Perform Approved Control or Functional Testing
steps.instructions: Use the facility-approved quality-control or functional verification process to determine whether the meter consistently detects an approved test sample. Do not substitute an unapproved material or bypass normal meter safeguards. Expected outcome: The meter completes repeated control or verification tests without sample-detection errors. If testing is consistently successful, document the findings and return the meter to service according to facility policy.

steps.title: 8. Compare With Another Meter
steps.instructions: When available, test the same approved control material using another known-good StatStrip meter. This helps distinguish a meter-specific problem from strip, control-material, handling, or environmental issues. Expected outcome: The comparison establishes whether the failure follows the suspect meter or the external materials. If the problem follows the consumable or test material rather than the meter, correct that external cause and stop after verification.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After any corrective action, perform multiple appropriate tests as permitted by facility procedure to confirm consistent strip recognition and sample detection. Inspect the display and strip port one final time. Expected outcome: The StatStrip consistently accepts strips, detects samples, and completes testing normally. If successful, the device may be returned to service following normal documentation requirements.

steps.title: 10. Remove From Service if Failures Continue
steps.instructions: If properly stored known-good strips, correct application, approved controls, and a clean undamaged strip port do not resolve the problem, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: An unreliable meter is prevented from returning to clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported that the StatStrip repeatedly failed to detect blood samples and required multiple test attempts.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found dried contamination around the external strip-port opening that interfered with consistent strip and sample detection.
CCR.Resolution: The meter was cleaned using the approved external procedure and successfully completed repeated control testing with known-good strips before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether multiple operators experienced the issue

title: Nova Biomedical StatStrip Blood Glucose Meter - Result Is Unexpected, Inconsistent, or Does Not Match a Comparison Method
description: Unexpected glucose results caused by sample differences, strip problems, contamination, test conditions, comparison timing, meter performance, or QC failure.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Care and Treat the Result as Unverified
steps.instructions: If a glucose result is inconsistent with the patient's condition or another measurement, clinical staff should obtain confirmation using another approved method before making decisions based solely on the questionable result. Do not troubleshoot the meter while it is being relied upon for active patient management. Expected outcome: Patient care proceeds using a verified result while the suspect meter is evaluated.

steps.title: 2. Clarify the Comparison
steps.instructions: Determine what the StatStrip result was compared against: another bedside meter, laboratory analyzer, blood gas analyzer, or repeat specimen. Record whether both samples were collected at approximately the same time and from comparable specimen sources. Expected outcome: The comparison is understood well enough to determine whether the values can reasonably be evaluated together.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Strip and Test Materials
steps.instructions: Verify the correct strip type, acceptable storage, clean handling, and absence of visible damage or contamination. Replace questionable strips with a known-good supply. Expected outcome: Strip condition is ruled out as an obvious source of inconsistent results. If consistent results return with known-good strips and control testing passes, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Meter for Contamination or Damage
steps.instructions: Check the strip port, housing, and surrounding surfaces for blood, liquid, cleaning residue, corrosion, cracks, or evidence of liquid intrusion. Do not perform deep disassembly or internal cleaning. Expected outcome: No visible condition exists that could interfere with strip connection or testing.

steps.title: 5. Perform Approved Quality-Control Testing
steps.instructions: Run the facility-approved QC materials according to established procedure. Do not adjust calibration or configuration merely to make the meter agree with another device. Expected outcome: QC results are acceptable according to the approved system criteria. If QC fails, remove the meter from clinical use until the cause is identified.

steps.title: 6. Compare With a Known-Good StatStrip
steps.instructions: Using the same approved control material, compare the suspect meter to another verified StatStrip when available. This avoids drawing conclusions from patient samples that may differ because of collection timing or specimen characteristics. Expected outcome: The suspect meter performs consistently with another verified meter during controlled testing.

steps.title: 7. Review Sample Collection Factors
steps.instructions: Confirm with clinical staff whether the discrepant result could have involved contamination, inadequate specimen collection, delayed testing, an unusual sample source, or another collection variable. Clinical Engineering should not diagnose the patient or interpret clinical significance. Expected outcome: Collection-related causes are either identified or reasonably excluded.

steps.title: 8. Check Date, Time, and Identification
steps.instructions: Verify that the result being compared belongs to the correct patient, operator, meter, date, and time. A mismatch in patient association or result timestamp can appear to be a measurement discrepancy. Expected outcome: Both values being compared are confirmed to refer to the intended patient and testing period.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Verification
steps.instructions: Run repeat approved controls or other manufacturer-authorized functional verification after correcting any identified external cause. Expected outcome: The meter produces repeatable, acceptable results under controlled conditions. If successful, troubleshooting may stop and the meter may be returned to service according to facility policy.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Measurement Discrepancies
steps.instructions: If known-good strips, proper QC, appropriate collection conditions, and controlled comparison testing still show unreliable meter performance, remove the device from service. Expected outcome: A potentially inaccurate meter is kept out of clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported that the StatStrip produced glucose results that differed significantly from repeated bedside measurements.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the suspect meter passed QC, but the reported comparison involved different specimen times and a questionable strip container.
CCR.Resolution: The questionable strips were removed from use, the meter passed repeated QC with known-good strips, and the unit was returned to service after verification.

title: Nova Biomedical StatStrip Blood Glucose Meter - Barcode Scanner Will Not Read Patient, Operator, or Strip Information
description: Barcode scanning failures caused by damaged labels, poor positioning, contamination, lighting, configuration, scanner-window damage, or meter communication problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Identification
steps.instructions: Do not allow a barcode problem to cause testing under the wrong patient or operator identity. If the facility permits an approved alternate identification workflow, clinical staff may use it. Otherwise, move testing to another verified meter. Expected outcome: Patient and operator identification remain accurate while troubleshooting proceeds.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Barcodes Fail
steps.instructions: Determine whether the scanner fails with patient wristbands, operator badges, strip information, or all barcode types. Record whether the scanner produces any illumination, tone, or response when activated. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to one barcode source or the scanner function generally.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Barcode
steps.instructions: Check the label for wrinkles, moisture, blood, fading, abrasion, glare, printing defects, or physical damage. Try another known-good barcode of the same type. Expected outcome: A clean, readable barcode is available for testing. If another barcode scans normally, the original label is the likely cause and meter troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 4. Clean and Inspect the Scanner Window
steps.instructions: Inspect the scanner window for fingerprints, blood, disinfectant residue, scratches, clouding, cracks, or moisture. Clean only using approved external methods. Expected outcome: The scanner window is clean, clear, and undamaged. If scanning returns to normal, perform final verification and stop.

steps.title: 5. Check Positioning and Lighting
steps.instructions: Test the scanner at reasonable distances and angles using a known-good barcode. Avoid severe glare or direct reflections that may interfere with scanning. Expected outcome: The scanner reliably reads when presented with a clear barcode under normal conditions.

steps.title: 6. Test Several Barcode Types
steps.instructions: When permitted, test known-good patient, operator, and applicable consumable barcodes. Determine whether one barcode format fails while others work normally. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to either a specific barcode type or the scanner itself.

steps.title: 7. Verify Approved Configuration
steps.instructions: Check only accessible, authorized configuration information related to barcode use. Do not change symbologies, security settings, or other configuration merely to experiment unless directed by approved institutional or manufacturer documentation. Expected outcome: The meter is configured for the barcode workflows intended by the facility.

steps.title: 8. Compare With Another Meter
steps.instructions: Scan the same barcode using another verified StatStrip. If the barcode also fails on the comparison meter, investigate the label or barcode-generation process rather than the suspect meter. Expected outcome: The comparison identifies whether the problem follows the barcode or the meter.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After cleaning, barcode replacement, or approved configuration correction, scan several known-good barcodes and confirm that the resulting identification information is correct on the meter. Expected outcome: Multiple barcodes scan consistently and populate the correct identification fields. If successful, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Remove From Service for Persistent Scanner Failure
steps.instructions: If known-good barcodes cannot be read despite a clean scanner window and correct approved configuration, remove the meter from service. Expected outcome: A meter with unreliable patient-identification capability is prevented from clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported that the StatStrip would not scan patient wristband barcodes.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found dried disinfectant residue obscuring the scanner window while known-good wristbands scanned normally after cleaning.
CCR.Resolution: The scanner window was cleaned using the approved method and multiple patient and operator barcodes were successfully verified before return to service.

title: Nova Biomedical StatStrip Blood Glucose Meter - Operator Login Fails or Authorized User Is Rejected
description: Login failures caused by badge problems, incorrect credentials, expired authorization, synchronization issues, configuration, or connectivity to the management system.

steps.title: 1. Maintain Testing Continuity
steps.instructions: If the operator cannot authenticate and patient glucose testing is required, use another verified meter or an approved alternate workflow according to facility policy. Do not bypass operator-security controls. Expected outcome: Testing continues without defeating access controls.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Login Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the operator is using barcode scanning, manual entry, or another approved authentication method. Record the exact displayed message without paraphrasing it into an invented error code. Expected outcome: The failure is documented accurately.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Operator Identity
steps.instructions: Confirm that the correct operator ID is being entered or scanned. Check for transposed digits, damaged badges, duplicate barcodes, or incorrect staff credentials. Expected outcome: The meter receives the intended operator identifier. If correcting the ID resolves access, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 4. Test the Operator on Another Meter
steps.instructions: Attempt authentication using another verified StatStrip in the same environment. Expected outcome: The comparison determines whether the rejection follows the operator account or the original meter. If the operator is rejected on multiple meters, investigate authorization or account status rather than meter hardware.

steps.title: 5. Test Another Authorized Operator
steps.instructions: Have a known-authorized user attempt login to the suspect meter. Expected outcome: Successful login by another user indicates that basic meter authentication is functioning. If only one operator is affected, escalate the account or authorization issue through the appropriate administrative process.

steps.title: 6. Check Date and Time
steps.instructions: Verify that the meter's date and time are reasonable and consistent with the facility system. Incorrect time may interfere with expiration, synchronization, or access-control logic. Expected outcome: Date and time are correct.

steps.title: 7. Verify Docking or Network Synchronization
steps.instructions: If operator authorization is centrally managed, confirm that the meter has recently docked or connected as required by the facility workflow. Inspect the dock and network path only within Clinical Engineering responsibility. Expected outcome: The meter is able to receive current authorization information.

steps.title: 8. Verify Approved Configuration
steps.instructions: Check accessible configuration related to the facility's operator-authentication workflow. Do not disable operator controls or make unauthorized security changes. Expected outcome: The meter is configured for the intended institutional authentication process.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Login Verification
steps.instructions: After synchronization, credential correction, or approved configuration correction, test login with an authorized operator and confirm that testing access is granted normally. Expected outcome: Authorized users can log in and unauthorized access controls remain intact. If successful, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Authentication Failure
steps.instructions: If multiple known-authorized operators are rejected on one meter despite correct date/time and successful synchronization, remove the meter from clinical use until evaluated. Expected outcome: A meter with unreliable access-control behavior is not returned to service.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported that an authorized operator was repeatedly rejected when attempting to log in to the StatStrip.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering confirmed the meter accepted other authorized users and found the affected operator authorization had not propagated to the meter.
CCR.Resolution: The meter was successfully synchronized through the approved workflow, the operator login was verified, and the meter was returned to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether other operators can log in
Whether the same operator works on another meter

title: Nova Biomedical StatStrip Blood Glucose Meter - Date and Time Incorrect or Reverts After Power Loss
description: Incorrect or resetting time caused by synchronization problems, power loss, configuration, docking issues, or a service-level clock-retention problem.

steps.title: 1. Protect Result Traceability
steps.instructions: If the meter displays substantially incorrect date or time, do not rely on it for patient testing until result timestamps can be trusted. Provide another verified meter if testing is required. Expected outcome: Patient results are not generated with unreliable timestamps.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Failure Pattern
steps.instructions: Determine whether the time is merely offset, progressively drifting, or resetting after battery depletion, shutdown, charging, or docking. Record the displayed date and time. Expected outcome: The problem pattern is clearly defined.

steps.title: 3. Compare With the Correct Facility Time
steps.instructions: Verify the current time using an approved facility reference. Check whether the meter differs by minutes, hours, date, or time zone. Expected outcome: The magnitude and type of time error are known.

steps.title: 4. Check Meter Power Status
steps.instructions: Inspect battery condition, charging behavior, and whether the meter recently experienced complete power loss. A power-related event may help explain when the clock changed. Expected outcome: Obvious power instability is ruled out or identified.

steps.title: 5. Verify Docking and Synchronization
steps.instructions: Place the meter on a known-good compatible dock according to normal workflow and confirm that it is detected. If time is centrally synchronized, allow the approved synchronization process to occur. Expected outcome: The meter communicates with the docking or management system and receives current information when designed to do so.

steps.title: 6. Compare With Another Meter
steps.instructions: Check the date and time on another StatStrip using the same dock or management environment. Expected outcome: The comparison helps determine whether the issue is meter-specific or system-wide. If multiple meters show the same incorrect time, investigate the central configuration or infrastructure.

steps.title: 7. Verify Authorized Time Configuration
steps.instructions: Review only accessible and approved configuration settings related to time or system synchronization. Do not make unsupported service-level configuration changes. Expected outcome: Time configuration agrees with the facility's intended setup.

steps.title: 8. Recheck After Power Cycling
steps.instructions: After synchronization and with adequate power, restart the meter normally and verify whether date and time are retained. Do not repeatedly power-cycle a meter being used clinically. Expected outcome: Correct time remains stable after a normal restart.

steps.title: 9. Perform a Retention Check
steps.instructions: After the meter has been disconnected from the dock and operated normally, recheck date and time. If appropriate, repeat after a normal shutdown and restart. Expected outcome: The correct clock setting is retained consistently. If successful, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate a Meter That Cannot Retain Time
steps.instructions: If date or time repeatedly resets despite correct synchronization and stable power, remove the meter from service. Expected outcome: Patient results are not generated with unreliable timestamps.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported that the StatStrip displayed the wrong date and time after being removed from the dock.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the meter had not synchronized correctly while using a malfunctioning docking station.
CCR.Resolution: The meter was synchronized on a known-good dock, date and time retention were verified through restart testing, and the meter was returned to service.

title: Nova Biomedical StatStrip Blood Glucose Meter - Meter Will Not Power On or Restarts During Testing
description: Power failures caused by depleted battery, charging problems, poor contacts, dock issues, contamination, physical damage, or service-level electrical faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Care
steps.instructions: Immediately replace a meter that shuts down or restarts during patient testing with another verified device. Do not continue troubleshooting an unreliable meter while a patient result is needed. Expected outcome: Patient testing continues without dependence on unstable equipment.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Power Symptom
steps.instructions: Determine whether the meter is completely dead, powers on only while docked, restarts randomly, restarts when a strip is inserted, or shuts down during testing. Expected outcome: The failure pattern is clearly defined.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for Physical or Liquid Damage
steps.instructions: Check the housing, display, battery area, charging contacts, and strip-port area for cracks, impact damage, moisture, corrosion, residue, swelling, heat damage, or odor. Expected outcome: No obvious unsafe physical condition is present. If liquid intrusion, swelling, overheating, or significant damage is found, stop troubleshooting and remove the meter from service.

steps.title: 4. Check Battery Condition and Installation
steps.instructions: Verify that the battery is correctly installed and that accessible battery contacts are clean and undamaged. Do not open sealed battery assemblies. Expected outcome: The battery is correctly seated with no visible damage.

steps.title: 5. Test With a Known-Good Charging Location
steps.instructions: Place the meter on a known-good compatible StatStrip docking station or charging location. Observe whether the meter shows expected charging or power behavior. Expected outcome: The meter recognizes external charging power.

steps.title: 6. Compare With Another Meter
steps.instructions: Place another known-good StatStrip on the same dock. If the second meter also fails to charge or power correctly, investigate the dock or its power source. Expected outcome: The fault is isolated to either the meter or charging infrastructure.

steps.title: 7. Allow Adequate Charging
steps.instructions: If the battery was depleted, allow charging according to approved facility and manufacturer practice before retesting. Do not repeatedly attempt patient testing on a meter with unstable power. Expected outcome: The meter powers on and remains stable after charging.

steps.title: 8. Perform Controlled Operational Testing
steps.instructions: Once adequately charged, power the meter on and navigate normal user-accessible functions. Insert an approved strip and perform permitted functional or control testing. Expected outcome: The meter remains powered throughout normal operation.

steps.title: 9. Verify Restart Behavior
steps.instructions: Observe the meter during repeated approved tests and while transitioning on and off the dock. Expected outcome: No unexpected shutdowns, resets, or boot cycles occur. If stable operation is demonstrated, troubleshooting may stop.

steps.title: 10. Remove From Service for Continued Instability
steps.instructions: If the meter will not power on or restarts despite known-good charging infrastructure and adequate battery charge, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: An electrically unreliable meter is kept out of patient care.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported that the StatStrip restarted intermittently while performing glucose tests.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the meter battery was not maintaining reliable power even when charged on a verified docking station.
CCR.Resolution: The meter was removed from service and sent for qualified repair, then passed repeated power and functional testing before return to service.

title: Nova Biomedical StatStrip Blood Glucose Meter - Test Strip Port Contaminated, Damaged, or Produces Repeated Errors
description: Strip-port problems caused by blood, disinfectant residue, debris, moisture, bent material, physical damage, or service-level strip-interface failure.

steps.title: 1. Remove an Unreliable Meter From Active Testing
steps.instructions: If the strip port is visibly damaged, wet, contaminated internally, or producing repeated test errors, replace the meter for ongoing patient testing. Expected outcome: Clinical testing continues on a reliable device.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Behavior
steps.instructions: Determine whether strips are difficult to insert, fail to register, disconnect intermittently, trigger repeated messages, or appear physically loose. Expected outcome: The strip-port symptom is clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Port Externally
steps.instructions: Under good lighting, examine the strip-port opening for blood, lint, dried residue, corrosion, foreign material, cracks, deformation, or signs of liquid intrusion. Do not insert probes, swabs, picks, or tools unless specifically permitted by approved manufacturer instructions. Expected outcome: The external condition of the strip port is known.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Test Strips
steps.instructions: Confirm that strips are flat, clean, dry, undamaged, and being inserted correctly. A damaged strip can resemble a meter-port failure. Expected outcome: Strip damage is ruled out.

steps.title: 5. Clean Only by Approved External Procedure
steps.instructions: If contamination is limited to externally accessible surfaces, clean and disinfect according to approved instructions. Allow the meter to dry completely before retesting. Expected outcome: Accessible contamination is removed without introducing additional moisture.

steps.title: 6. Test With Known-Good Strips
steps.instructions: Use a known-good strip supply and observe insertion, recognition, and retention. Do not force a strip into a resistant or visibly damaged port. Expected outcome: The meter consistently recognizes properly inserted strips.

steps.title: 7. Compare With Another Meter
steps.instructions: Insert a strip from the same known-good supply into another StatStrip. This helps distinguish strip-lot or handling issues from a port-specific problem. Expected outcome: The fault follows either the suspect meter or the consumables.

steps.title: 8. Perform Approved Control Testing
steps.instructions: If the port appears intact and recognizes strips, complete approved QC or functional testing. Expected outcome: Testing completes without repeated strip-related errors. If the meter passes repeated testing, troubleshooting may stop.

steps.title: 9. Reinspect After Testing
steps.instructions: Remove the strip and confirm that no unusual resistance, looseness, debris, or visible damage developed during testing. Expected outcome: The strip port remains mechanically intact and clean.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Physical or Persistent Port Problems
steps.instructions: If the port is cracked, deformed, loose, corroded, repeatedly loses strip recognition, or cannot be safely cleaned externally, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: A meter with an unreliable strip interface is removed from clinical service.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported repeated strip errors and intermittent strip recognition on the StatStrip.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found dried blood residue around the accessible strip-port opening while the port showed no visible structural damage.
CCR.Resolution: The meter was cleaned using the approved procedure and passed repeated strip-recognition and control testing before return to service.

title: Nova Biomedical StatStrip Blood Glucose Meter - Result Will Not Transmit to the Patient Record After Docking
description: Missing result transmission caused by docking, patient association, network connectivity, synchronization, interface, configuration, or downstream system problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Clinical Documentation
steps.instructions: Confirm that the glucose result remains available on the meter and that clinical staff have an approved method to document or verify the result while transmission is being investigated. Do not repeat patient testing solely because an interface failed unless clinically necessary. Expected outcome: The result remains traceable and patient care is not delayed.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Missing Result
steps.instructions: Identify the patient, result time, meter, and whether the result appears locally on the StatStrip. Confirm whether one result, several results, or all results are affected. Expected outcome: The transmission failure is clearly scoped.

steps.title: 3. Verify Patient Identification
steps.instructions: Confirm that the affected test was associated with the intended patient identifier. A result with incomplete or incorrect patient association may not route to the record as expected. Expected outcome: Patient identification is correct and complete.

steps.title: 4. Confirm Docking
steps.instructions: Place the meter securely in the intended dock and verify that the dock physically detects the meter. Inspect charging and data-contact areas for dirt, damage, or poor seating. Expected outcome: The meter is correctly seated and recognized by the dock.

steps.title: 5. Test the Dock With Another Meter
steps.instructions: Dock a known-good StatStrip using the same station. Determine whether that meter communicates normally. Expected outcome: The test identifies whether the issue follows the dock or the original meter.

steps.title: 6. Test the Meter on Another Dock
steps.instructions: If available, dock the suspect meter on a known-good compatible station. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to the meter, dock, or local infrastructure. If the result transmits normally from another dock, troubleshoot the original docking location rather than the meter.

steps.title: 7. Check Network and Infrastructure
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible network connections, link status, power, and local data path associated with the docking station. Do not change network addressing or interface configuration without authorization. Expected outcome: The dock has the infrastructure required for communication.

steps.title: 8. Verify Synchronization and System Status
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the meter shows evidence of successful communication or synchronization using normal accessible indicators. Determine whether other StatStrip meters are also unable to send results. Expected outcome: A meter-specific issue is distinguished from a broader middleware, network, or electronic medical record interface issue.

steps.title: 9. Perform End-to-End Verification
steps.instructions: Using an approved test workflow, verify that a new test result from the meter is transmitted through the expected interface and appears in the appropriate receiving system. Use appropriate non-patient testing procedures where required by policy. Expected outcome: A new result successfully reaches the intended destination. If successful, troubleshooting may stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Unresolved Transmission Failures
steps.instructions: If the meter and dock communicate locally but results still fail to reach the patient record, escalate to the appropriate interface, middleware, laboratory, network, or information-systems support team. Expected outcome: The unresolved portion of the communication path is handed to the responsible service group.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported that completed StatStrip glucose results remained on the meter but did not appear in the patient record after docking.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the meter transmitted normally on a known-good dock and isolated the failure to the original docking station's network connection.
CCR.Resolution: The docking-station network connection was restored, end-to-end result transmission was verified, and the station was returned to service.

title: Nova Biomedical StatStrip Blood Glucose Meter - Docking Station Has No Power or Does Not Detect the Meter
description: Docking failures caused by AC power, loose connections, dirty contacts, poor seating, damaged docks, meter contacts, or network and communication problems.

steps.title: 1. Maintain Meter Availability
steps.instructions: Move the StatStrip to another verified charging or docking location if needed so battery depletion or missed synchronization does not interrupt patient testing. Expected outcome: Clinical glucose testing remains available while the dock is evaluated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Docking Symptom
steps.instructions: Determine whether the station is completely unpowered, powers on but does not recognize meters, charges without communicating, or communicates intermittently. Expected outcome: The problem is narrowed to power, detection, charging, or communication.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Dock and Power Supply
steps.instructions: Check the docking station, power supply, cord, connectors, and housing for cracks, loose connections, liquid contamination, damaged insulation, bent contacts, heat, or odor. Expected outcome: No obvious unsafe physical defect is present. If there is significant damage, overheating, or liquid intrusion, remove the dock from service immediately.

steps.title: 4. Verify AC Power
steps.instructions: Confirm that the dock's power connection is secure. Test the outlet using an approved method or connect the dock to a known-good appropriate power source if permitted. Expected outcome: Reliable AC power is available to the dock.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Dock Contacts
steps.instructions: Check accessible meter-contact areas for dirt, dried disinfectant, corrosion, debris, or physical damage. Clean only using approved external procedures. Expected outcome: Contact areas are clean, dry, and intact.

steps.title: 6. Reseat the Meter
steps.instructions: Place the meter firmly into the dock according to its normal orientation and observe whether charging or communication begins. Expected outcome: Correct seating produces normal meter detection.

steps.title: 7. Test Another Meter
steps.instructions: Place a known-good StatStrip in the suspect docking station. Expected outcome: The test identifies whether the failure follows the dock or the original meter.

steps.title: 8. Test the Meter in Another Dock
steps.instructions: Place the original meter into a known-good compatible docking station. Expected outcome: The problem is further isolated between the meter and dock.

steps.title: 9. Check Data Connectivity
steps.instructions: If the dock powers and charges normally but does not communicate, inspect accessible network connections and link status. Avoid unauthorized network or configuration changes. Expected outcome: Required physical data connections are intact.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm with a known-good meter that the dock powers, detects the meter, charges when applicable, and communicates through the expected workflow. Expected outcome: Docking operation is stable and repeatable. If successful, troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported that the StatStrip docking station did not detect meters and provided no charging indication.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the docking-station power connection loose while the outlet and meter tested normally.
CCR.Resolution: The power connection was secured and the dock successfully detected, charged, and communicated with a known-good meter before return to service.

title: Nova Biomedical StatStrip Blood Glucose Meter - Cleaning or Disinfection Damage to Housing, Display, or Strip Port
description: Damage after cleaning or disinfection, including cracks, clouding, residue, liquid intrusion, degraded controls, display problems, or strip-port contamination.

steps.title: 1. Remove Questionable Equipment From Patient Use
steps.instructions: If cleaning damage affects the display, housing integrity, strip port, controls, electrical safety, or ability to disinfect the meter, remove it from clinical use. Provide another verified meter. Expected outcome: A physically compromised meter is not used for patient testing.

steps.title: 2. Confirm What Changed After Cleaning
steps.instructions: Determine what cleaning or disinfection event preceded the problem and what symptom followed. Document whether the issue involves clouding, cracks, discoloration, sticky controls, unreadable display areas, liquid in openings, or strip-port errors. Expected outcome: The observed damage and its timing are documented.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Housing
steps.instructions: Check all accessible exterior surfaces for cracks, separation, swelling, softened material, discoloration, missing labels, degraded seals, or sharp edges. Expected outcome: Housing integrity is clearly assessed. If the housing no longer protects the meter or cannot be safely disinfected, stop troubleshooting and remove it from service.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Display and Controls
steps.instructions: Check the display for clouding, dark areas, loss of contrast, touch or button problems, moisture beneath the surface, or cleaning residue. Expected outcome: The display remains readable and controls respond consistently.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Strip Port
steps.instructions: Look for moisture, residue, corrosion, debris, cracks, or softened material around the strip-port opening. Do not probe or perform internal cleaning. Expected outcome: The strip port is dry, clean, and structurally intact.

steps.title: 6. Allow the Meter to Dry When Appropriate
steps.instructions: If the problem appears limited to external residual moisture and there is no evidence of internal liquid intrusion, allow the meter to dry using approved handling practices. Do not use unapproved heat sources or compressed air. Expected outcome: Residual external moisture is eliminated without further damage.

steps.title: 7. Clean Residue Using the Approved Procedure
steps.instructions: If visible residue is present on approved external surfaces, reclean the meter using the facility-approved and manufacturer-compatible method. Avoid excessive liquid application. Expected outcome: Residue is removed without affecting the housing, display, or strip port.

steps.title: 8. Perform Functional Testing
steps.instructions: Power on the meter and verify display readability, controls, barcode scanning if applicable, strip recognition, and approved QC or functional testing. Expected outcome: All affected external functions work consistently. If all functions are normal and no structural damage remains, troubleshooting may stop after documentation.

steps.title: 9. Evaluate Cleanability
steps.instructions: Even if the meter operates electrically, verify that damaged surfaces can still be adequately cleaned and disinfected. Cracked, delaminated, or degraded surfaces may make the device unsuitable for continued clinical use. Expected outcome: The meter remains physically suitable for safe infection-control practices.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Permanent or Internal Damage
steps.instructions: If cleaning has caused cracking, liquid intrusion, corrosion, unreadable display areas, unreliable controls, strip-port failure, or surfaces that cannot be properly disinfected, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: A compromised meter is removed from circulation.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported that the StatStrip display became cloudy and the strip port began producing intermittent errors after cleaning.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found excess dried cleaning residue around the display edges and accessible strip-port opening with no evidence of structural cracking or internal liquid intrusion.
CCR.Resolution: The meter was recleaned using the approved procedure, allowed to dry, and successfully passed display, strip-recognition, and control testing before return to service.
